newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business News - August 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business News - August 6.

DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- USERS OF TV GADGET FACING 5,000 STERLING FINE

The government has made a call to ban a popular television accessory, the video sender, which allows households with multiple televisions, but only one video recorder, cable television or satellite decoder to send pictures to any TV in the house. The ban is being sought due to the government fears the devices may interfere with the reception of neighbours' televisions and may affect emergency services' radio transmissions. From September 1, it will be illegal to possess, sell, or manufacture video sende rs in the UK.
-- AMSTRAD INVESTORS TO SHARE DAMAGES

Distressed debt specialist Klesh & Co. has announced it will set up a secondary market to allow shareholders in Alan Sugar's now defunct Amstrad computer group to trade the litigation certificates they received in the break up of Amstrad which entitle them to a portion of the 86m stg in damages won by the group from Seagate Technology. The vouchers, which will be printed and made available next week, also entitle shareholders to a share of any payout stemming from the legal battle with Western Digital Corporation.
-- CASTLE WINS 200M STG CONTRACT WITH BDB

Castle Transmission, which earlier in the year acquired the BBC's domestic transmission network, has been awarded a 200m stg contract to transmit for the British Digital Broadcasting consortium and an additional contract to transmit the BBC digital multiplex. Castle will begin work on the BDB networks next year and hope to have work completed by 1999. Castle beat out NTL, which owns the ITV transmission network and will be constructing the digital networks for ITV, Channel 4 and S4C.
THE TIMES
-- SIMON TO SELL 2.3M STG BP SHARES

Minister for trade and competitiveness for Europe, Lord Simon of Highbury, and former chairman of BP, has bowed to political pressure concerning a conflict of interests and announced the sale of his 2.3 million sterling worth of shares in BP. Lord Simon also vowed to donate to charity the 350,000 stg profit he made on the shares since becoming minister, as BP share prices rose yesterday by 39.5p on the strength of second-quarter results.
-- SMITHS AGREES 136M STG BID FOR RIVAL GRASEBY

Aerospace to medical supplies group Smiths Industries has acquired its rival, Graseby, for 136m stg in a deal expected to create the largest mobile drug pump company in the world. Graseby manufactures three models of the take-home belts, which automatically administer controlled doses of drugs, while Smiths manufactures just one. Both companies are aiming at the US, European and Far East markets and have made plans to bid for the $400m JCAD US toxic chemicals detector contract to be issued by the armed forces.
-- BT IN TALKS OVER JOB CUTS

British Telecommunications will meet with leaders of the Communications Workers Union to discuss the telecoms giant's plans to axe its workforce by up to 5,000 next April. The CWU has complained BT provided a lack of consultation over the redundancies, and has also taken opposition to its increasing use of contract workers for work which had previously been carried out by BT staff. BT staff in London have planned a strike next Tuesday in protest of the use of contract workers.
THE GUARDIAN
-- GEC CHIEF POACHES FELLOW SCOT FROM ZENECA AS FINANCE BOSS

GEC managing director George Simpson has hired Zeneca's finance director, John Mayo, as his company's new finance director. Mayo earned 611,000 stg in 1996 at Zeneca, and his payrise is expected to further increase at GEC. Mayo will also gain over $2.3m from exercising his share options in Zeneca when he leaves in October. The appointment furthers the management shake-up at GEC, as Mayo will replace David Newlands, who left as a result of the overhaul.
-- MURDOCH TAKES AN HISTORIC CHARGE

HarperCollins, the book publishers owned by media magnate Rupert Murdoch, are to take a $270m charge to cover costs created by losses from author advances, inventories of unsold books and job cuts. The $270m cut is the largest in the history of publishing, but the News Corporation president says he has no plans to sell the publishing arm, as it 'is a very important part of the company's assets'.
-- GLAXO FEELS TIP TOP

Shares in pharmaceutical group Glaxo Wellcome experienced a substantial rise on Monday, after it was revealed two rival groups had signed on to market generic versions of Glaxo's Zantac anti-ulcer treatment drug. While the deal between Genpharm and Novopharm ends Glaxo's monopoly on Zantac, it has been determined the best method for the drugs giant to deal with spiralling prices and fears of a 'free for all' market.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- RAIL FIRM OFFERS BONUS TO CANCEL HOLIDAYS

London's South West Trains has offered to pay any member of its staff 1,500 sterling per week to relinquish their holidays so they will be able to work through the summer. SWT stated the majority of its employees take their vacation time in the summer, and unless such an incentive is offered, the company will be forced to cancel numerous trains. The Health and Safety Executive has called the scheme into question and will investigate if any breaches of safety rules are therein contained.
-- PEARSON ON TRACK TO BUY 'THOMAS'

Pearson has emerged as the favoured candidate to acquire the children's book division of Reed, which publishes popular titles such as Winnie the Pooh and Thomas the Tank Engine. Should Pearson acquire the division, it would be the group's first UK deal under new chief executive Marjorie Scardino, and it would be merged with Pearson's Penguin subsidiary.
-- BP FANS STRIKE IT RICH WITH SHARE BUY-BACK

British Petroleum has formally announced its long-awaited share buy-back incentive, which is expected to begin following approval at its next annual meeting in May. BP, on Monday, also revealed its half-year profits had increased 21 per cent to 2.437bn and exploration and production profits up from 1.49bn to 1.6bn and that it had once again beaten its internal efficiency targets. The series of announcements led BP shares to soar 39.5p to a 12-month high of 862.5p. For a full range of news monitoring services, phone BMC "44-171-377-1742
